title: Secure GET /users with SQLite field whitelist and safe errors
summary: Hardened GET /users to read from SQLite with a static parameterized query, explicit PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS serialization, generic client errors with correlation IDs, and server-side exception logging.

threats_mitigated.description: Dynamic SQL built from request input could allow injection into the users table read path.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Static SELECT with fixed columns; no user input in the query. Seed inserts use executemany with ? placeholders.

threats_mitigated.threat_name: Sensitive field disclosure in API responses
threats_mitigated.description: Returning full row dicts could expose password hashes or internal columns if the schema grows.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS whitelist and serialize_user() project only id, username, email into JSON.

threats_mitigated.description: SQLite stack traces or error text in HTTP responses reveal schema and implementation details.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: Catch sqlite3.Error, log server-side with correlation_id, return generic JSON error body without SQL or trace text.

threats_mitigated.description: Unhandled exceptions could leave SQLite connections open under load.
threats_mitigated.mitigation_applied: finally block always closes the connection.

best_practices_achieved: Parameterized/static SQL for all database reads
Explicit response field whitelist separate from DB projection
Generic user-facing errors with opaque correlation IDs
Server-side exception logging without echoing secrets
Deterministic ORDER BY id for stable list responses
Automated tests for happy path and error non-disclosure

secure_code_snippets.explanation: Whitelist serializer ensures only public fields reach the client even if the query changes.
Static parameterized read with safe error handling and connection cleanup.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not build queries or commands with string concatenation
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't concatenate untrusted input into SQL/NoSQL/LDAP/OS command templates. Use parameterized APIs and safe query builders.
guardrails_applied.notes: GET /users uses a static SELECT; seed data uses ? placeholders via executemany.

guardrails_applied.title: Use parameter binding with SQLAlchemy or raw cursors
guardrails_applied.instruction: Execute raw queries as db.session.execute(text('... :id'), {'id': ...}); never f-string.
guardrails_applied.notes: sqlite3 execute/executemany with bound parameters; no f-string SQL on the /users path.

guardrails_applied.title: Do not use jsonify with SQLAlchemy model objects directly
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't dump full model dicts via jsonify(user.__dict__); build an explicit response dict or use a marshmallow schema.
guardrails_applied.notes: serialize_user builds an explicit dict from PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS instead of dict(row).

guardrails_applied.title: Do not return verbose internal errors to users
guardrails_applied.instruction: Don't expose stack traces, SQL errors, framework debug pages, or internal identifiers in responses. Return generic errors with correlation IDs.
guardrails_applied.notes: 500 responses return a fixed error string plus correlation_id; SQL text never included.

guardrails_applied.title: Eliminate vulnerability classes structurally, not by case-by-case patching
guardrails_applied.instruction: For each class CISA highlights (SQLi, XSS, command injection, path traversal, memory-safety bugs), pick a structural mitigation rather than per-callsite review: parameterized queries / ORM-only DB access.
guardrails_applied.notes: Structural field whitelist and static query pattern applied to the listing endpoint.
